text: Right now, somewhere in India, a mother has walked for hours to reach a health centre. The medicine her child needs ran out days ago. And the district won't find out for a month.
India's primary healthcare runs on twenty five thousand health centres, and paper registers. The data reaches the district in monthly reports. By then, patients have already been turned away.
So we built HealthGrid AI. Today's systems record what happened. HealthGrid decides what to do next.
It starts with a voice. No forms. A health worker holds one button, and speaks.

Gnani's speech engine understands Hindi, Marathi, English, even all of them mixed together. Gemini turns those words into a structured update. The worker confirms it. And the whole district reacts, in seconds.
This is what the district health officer sees. Every facility, scored live. Not just what's wrong, but exactly why.
Then it acts. A centre is running out of medicine? HealthGrid finds a nearby centre with surplus, checks the safety limits, and proposes a transfer. One click from a human, and it's done.
Alerts reach the frontline on WhatsApp. And when a flood or a heatwave is coming, HealthGrid re-plans the district before the shortage arrives.
Every number comes from tested, deterministic engines. The AI explains. Humans decide.
No new hardware. No rip and replace. One district to prove it. The National Health Mission to fund it. And a path to every district in India.
We won Google Cloud's Build with AI in Smart Health. Now, we're looking for partners to take HealthGrid into its first real district.
Because often, the medicine is already in the district. It's just in the wrong place. HealthGrid fixes that.
